goldens.comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
goldens.reasoning: C1 points out that backup code checking is case-sensitive, so uppercase codes get rejected.

goldens.comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate mentions the race condition when the same code is used concurrently.

goldens.comment: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
goldens.reasoning: C2 points out that the Blob URL is not revoked on unmount, which leaks memory.

candidates: Backup code verification only strips dashes and is case-sensitive; generated codes are lowercase hex while the UI suggests uppercase, causing users pasting uppercase codes or codes with whitespace to be incorrectly rejected
EnableTwoFactorModal creates a Blob URL for downloading backup codes but doesn't revoke it on close/reset/unmount, leaving a live URL and retaining memory with sensitive content longer than necessary

Login form disables browser validation (noValidate) and the schema doesn't require backupCode; submitting the backup-code screen empty can re-set twoFactorRequired without showing a useful error, leaving users stuck
